name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that overlays the dark theme’s text and background. It catches low-contrast text instantly, preventing unreadable submissions. The trade-off is a small performance hit from real-time checks, but it guarantees readability—no other fix is as fast or reliable.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker trains users to ignore the problem—once they see the crap contrast in real time, they’ll just hit submit anyway, thinking it’s “good enough.” A better alternative is a pre-submission block that forces a fix before moving forward; it’s slower upfront but stops bad submissions before they happen. Settle it with a quick A/B test: half the users get the live checker, half get the block—measure drop-off rates and final contrast scores.

name: Pane
text: The pre-submission block risks user drop-off—users won’t tolerate being blocked mid-flow for a fix they can’t immediately see the value of. A better alternative is a hybrid: flag low-contrast text in real time but require a manual override confirmation before submission, balancing speed with enforcement. Settle it with A/B testing—measure drop-off rates and final contrast compliance between the two approaches.
